Stand down on new credit spreads today or push DTE past the yield-shock window. Cash is a position.

focus.jbig: Bond-yield shock resets the tape · risk-off · stand down
focus.jtag: 10Y hits 5.11% (highest since 2007) on strong PMIs and a weak auction; futures fall and two of three boarded breakouts (META, AMD) are already gapping down
focus.jnote: The environment changed overnight — and not for premium sellers. On Wednesday, strong S&P Global PMI data plus a weak 5-year Treasury auction pushed yields to multi-decade highs, with the 10-year hitting ~5.11% (highest since 2007), the 2-year near 4.90% and the 30-year at a post-2004 peak. The Dow fell 0.68%, the S&P 500 0.75% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.13%, led lower by communication services, utilities and consumer discretionary. Futures are lower again Thursday — Nasdaq-100 ~−1% — and chips (NVDA, AMD, INTC) are extending declines pre-market. Trump–Xi meet Thursday and the US-China trade truce was extended two months, but rate fear is dominating. This is a rising-rate, risk-off tape — not one to sell fresh bull puts into.
focus.notdown: Media/M&A (WBD) is the one boarded name still holding a bid — it’s pinned near its 52-week high on the Paramount merger settlement (deal expected to close in ~two weeks, with a ticking fee accruing to WBD). But be honest: this is a deal-closing reprice, not a durable technical trend, and on a risk-off day even a merger name can drift. Watch, size small, confirm at 9:35.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive tech & chips (META, AMD, NVDA, INTC) are the pressure point — higher yields hit long-duration growth hardest, and META and AMD are both gapping down pre-market, back toward their breakout pivots. Selling bull puts into names that are actively failing their breakout is exactly what 4-VAL exists to stop. But shorting them via bear calls into a possible relief-bounce carries squeeze risk too — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite jumped to 62 (deep WARM) and P(≥1% gap) at ~38% is above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: a disorderly bond sell-off to 2007-high yields is an open-ended macro shock that can gap the whole tape on the next auction, data print or Fed comment. And the board itself is failing: two of three boarded breakouts (META, AMD) are gapping DOWN, invalidating the bull-put thesis before the open. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the yield-shock window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: The scanner boarded WBD Type C on a 52-week/all-time-high breakout that has HELD 2 sessions above the ~$28.90 pivot; it copies through at Grade A. Honest caveats: this is a merger-reprice catalyst, not a durable technical trend, with only 1 S/R layer (pivot ~$28.90, −6.2%). Liquidity screened OK (ATM spread $0.01, OI 17,495). Next earnings ~Nov 5 is outside DTE. It’s the one boarded name still holding a bid on a risk-off morning.

Rate-hike repricing — multi-year highs in PMI input/output prices have markets betting on another Fed hike this year. A hawkish Fed comment or hot data point would compound the sell-off.

Two of three boarded breakouts failing — META and AMD are gapping DOWN through/toward their pivots pre-market. Run 4-VAL on each at 9:35; if price is below prior close and the open, INVALIDATE — do not sell a bull put into a failing breakout.
Trump–Xi meeting (Thu) — the US-China truce was extended two months, but the meeting outcome, critical minerals and AI-chip export policy are live wires that can gap the tape either way.

WBD merger headline risk — WBD is pinned to its high entirely on the Paramount deal-close probability; any settlement or regulatory setback gaps it down regardless of the tape. Verify at 9:35 before any entry.
